source: Products neurodivergent people and families recommend; each checked on its maker's or seller's own pages (.qa-local/products/BRIEF.md): every quality has a quote from those pages, in quality_evidence

entries.name: Unmasking Autism
entries.description: A guide for autistic adults who mask or found out late, written by an autistic social psychologist. It mixes his own story with research, profiles of other autistic people and exercises for unmasking.

quality_evidence.own_voices: is a social psychologist, professor, author, and proud Autistic person

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the hardcover at $37.99 and the new paperback at $24.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: A deep dive into the spectrum of Autistic experience and the phenomenon of masked Autism, giving individuals the tools to safely uncover their true selves
entries.notes: Published by Harmony (Penguin Random House), 2022. The 320-page paperback is a pre-order on Indigo until 20 October 2026; the hardcover (304 pages), ebook and Kobo audiobook are available now.

entries.name: How to ADHD
entries.description: A practical guide to working with an ADHD brain, by the creator of the How to ADHD YouTube channel, who was diagnosed at twelve. It collects the strategies she learned from experts and from her own life.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Diagnosed with ADHD at age twelve

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $29.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: In this honest, friendly, and shame-free guide, the creator of the award-winning YouTube channel How to ADHD shares the hard-won insights and practical strategies
entries.notes: Published by Rodale Books (Penguin Random House). McCabe also runs the How to ADHD YouTube channel, which the book grew out of.

entries.name: ADHD 2.0
entries.brand: Edward M. Hallowell and John J. Ratey
entries.description: A short guide to ADHD in children and adults by two psychiatrists who have ADHD themselves. It treats ADHD as a trait with upsides as well as challenges and gives everyday strategies.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Two psychiatrists who have ADHD themselves

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $27.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: A revolutionary new approach to ADD/ADHD featuring cutting-edge research and strategies to help readers thrive
entries.notes: Published by Ballantine Books (Penguin Random House). The authors also wrote Driven to Distraction. Its strategies include medication alongside lifestyle changes.

entries.name: Look Me in the Eye
entries.description: A memoir by John Elder Robison, who was diagnosed autistic at forty, about growing up feeling different, building guitars for KISS and raising a family. Told with dark humour.

quality_evidence.own_voices: It was not until he was forty that he was diagnosed with a form of autism called Asperger’s syndrome.

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $23.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: A born storyteller, Robison has written a moving, darkly funny memoir about a life that has taken him from developing exploding guitars for KISS to building a family of his own.
entries.notes: Published by Crown (Penguin Random House). It uses the older term Asperger’s. Robison is the neurodiversity scholar in residence at the College of William & Mary, per the publisher.

entries.name: Strong Female Character
entries.description: A frank, funny memoir by Scottish comedian Fern Brady about being diagnosed autistic at thirty-four after years of being told she could not be autistic. Suits adults, especially autistic women.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Fern Brady knew instinctively that she had it—autism explained her sensory issues, her meltdowns, her inability to pick up on social cues

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the hardcover at $37.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: In this frank and surreal memoir, she delivers a sharp and often hilarious portrait of neurodivergence and living unmasked.
entries.notes: Published by Harmony (Penguin Random House). For adults: the publisher’s summary mentions a psychiatric stay, stripping and an arrest.

entries.name: I Overcame My Autism and All I Got Was This Lousy Anxiety Disorder
entries.description: A funny, critical memoir by autistic Canadian writer Sarah Kurchak about growing up undiagnosed in small-town Ontario, masking to avoid bullying, and what would make autistic lives better. For adults.

quality_evidence.canadian: Growing up undiagnosed in small-town Ontario in the eighties and nineties

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Douglas & McIntyre listed the paperback at $24.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Kurchak’s enlightening memoir challenges stereotypes and preconceptions about autism and considers what might really make the lives of autistic people healthier, happier and more fulfilling.
entries.notes: Published by Douglas & McIntyre in 2020. The title is tongue-in-cheek: the book questions the idea of an autistic “success story”.

entries.name: Ten Steps to Nanette
entries.description: A memoir by the Australian comedian behind the show Nanette, covering growing up queer in Tasmania, their path into comedy, and being diagnosed with autism and ADHD as an adult.

quality_evidence.own_voices: their struggle with late-in-life diagnoses of autism and ADHD

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $27.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Harrowing and hilarious, Ten Steps to Nanette traces Gadsby’s growth as a queer person, their ever-evolving relationship with comedy, and their struggle with late-in-life diagnoses of autism and ADHD
entries.notes: Published by Ballantine Books (Penguin Random House). For adults: the publisher’s summary mentions homophobic and sexual violence.

entries.name: Thinking in Pictures, Expanded Edition
entries.description: Temple Grandin’s account of her life as an autistic scientist and of how she thinks in pictures rather than words. This edition adds a new afterword with updated research and tips.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Grandin writes from the dual perspectives of a scientist and an autistic person

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $25.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Originally published in 1995 as an unprecedented look at autism, Grandin writes from the dual perspectives of a scientist and an autistic person to give a report from “the country of autism.”
entries.notes: Published by Vintage (Penguin Random House), with a foreword by Oliver Sacks. First published in 1995, so some of its framing of autism is older.

entries.name: A Kind of Spark
entries.description: A middle-grade novel about Addie, an autistic girl in a small Scottish town who campaigns for a memorial to the women once burned as witches there. Written by an autistic author; for readers about 9 to 12.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Award-winning and neurodivergent author Elle McNicoll
quality_evidence.nd_character: I’m autistic. I see things that others do not.

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $12.50 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: a neurodivergent girl campaigns for a memorial when she learns that her small Scottish town used to burn witches simply because they were different.
entries.notes: Published in North America by Yearling (Penguin Random House); a Schneider Family Honor title, per the publisher. Grades 3 to 7.

entries.name: Bookmarks Are People Too! (Here’s Hank #1)
entries.description: The first Here’s Hank early-reader chapter book, about a second-grader who struggles with spelling and reading, printed in an easy-to-read font. Co-written by Henry Winkler, who is dyslexic; for ages 6 to 8.

quality_evidence.own_voices: whose undiagnosed dyslexia made him a classic childhood underachiever
quality_evidence.nd_character: a boy with learning differences

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $10.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: In the first book of this bestselling easy-to-read series, Hank tries out for the second-grade class play!
entries.notes: Published by Penguin Workshop. Here’s Hank is the early-reader prequel to Hank Zipzer; the page says the series is about a boy with learning differences rather than naming dyslexia in this book.

entries.name: Wonderfully Wired Brains
entries.description: An illustrated children’s guide to neurodiversity that explains different kinds of brains, busts myths and introduces neurodivergent advocates. Written by a neurodivergent author, with a font and colours chosen for neurodivergent readers.

quality_evidence.own_voices: written by neurodiverse author Louise Gooding
quality_evidence.plain_language: The font and colors used have been selected to accommodate a range of neurodiverse readers.
quality_evidence.audiobook: audiobook written and read by neurodiverse author Louise Gooding

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the hardcover at $24.50 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: An informative and inclusive children’s guide to neurodiversity for those not in the know and to inspire children who are neurodivergent.
entries.notes: Published by DK Children. The publisher says ages 7 to 9 (Grades 2 to 4); Indigo lists it for ages 6 to 8. The audiobook is a separate edition, read by the author.

entries.name: Funny, You Don’t Look Autistic
entries.description: A funny memoir for teens by stand-up comic Michael McCreary, who was diagnosed autistic at five, about school, sensory life and comedy. For readers 12 and up, autistic or not.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Diagnosed with ASD at age five, McCreary got hit with the performance bug not much later.

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Annick Press and Indigo listed the paperback at $14.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: This unique and hilarious #OwnVoices memoir breaks down what it’s like to live with autism for readers on and off the spectrum.
entries.notes: Published by Annick Press; joint winner of the Canadian Children’s Book Centre’s Best Books for Kids & Teens 2019, per Annick. Indigo tags it Canadian. Uses the term ASD.

entries.name: Planet Earth Is Blue
entries.description: A middle-grade novel about Nova, a nonspeaking autistic girl in foster care who loves space and counts down to the Challenger launch and to seeing her sister again. For readers about 9 to 12.

quality_evidence.nd_character: the extraordinary mind of a young girl with autism

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $12.50 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: While foster families and teachers dismiss Nova as severely autistic and nonverbal, Bridget understands how intelligent and special Nova is, and all that she can’t express.
entries.notes: Published by Yearling (Penguin Random House); Grades 3 to 7. Deals with foster care and family separation.

entries.name: The Many Mysteries of the Finkel Family
entries.description: A middle-grade mystery about two autistic sisters, a detective agency and a strained friendship; one sister uses her tablet to talk. For readers about 9 to 12.

quality_evidence.nd_character: two autistic sisters

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the hardcover at $23.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: meet the Finkel family in this middle grade novel about two autistic sisters, their detective agency, and life’s most consequential mysteries.
entries.notes: Published by Dial Books (Penguin Random House). The author is active in the disability rights and neurodiversity movements, per the publisher.

entries.name: Fish in a Tree
entries.description: A middle-grade novel about Ally, a sixth-grader who hides that she cannot read until a new teacher helps her find out she is dyslexic. For readers about 9 to 12.

quality_evidence.nd_character: the recognition of her dyslexia

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $13.99 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Every time she lands in a new school, she is able to hide her inability to read by creating clever yet disruptive distractions.
entries.notes: Published by Nancy Paulsen Books (Penguin Random House). The publisher’s page does not say the author is dyslexic.

entries.name: The Dyslexic Advantage (Revised and Updated)
entries.brand: Brock L. Eide and Fernette F. Eide
entries.description: A strengths-based guide to dyslexia by two physicians who run the nonprofit Dyslexic Advantage. It explains dyslexic thinking, profiles dyslexic people and is written for parents, educators and dyslexic adults.

quality_evidence.for_parents: valuable new insights for educators, employers, parents, dyslexic adults
quality_evidence.for_adults: valuable new insights for educators, employers, parents, dyslexic adults

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $28.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: debunk the standard deficit-based approach to dyslexia
entries.notes: Published by Plume (Penguin Random House). Indigo also sells the 2012 first edition under a similar title; this entry is the revised edition. The authors are not described as dyslexic.

entries.name: The Kiss Quotient
entries.description: A romance about Stella Lane, a woman with Asperger’s who is great with data and decides she needs practice with dating. Written by an author who was diagnosed autistic as an adult; for adults.

quality_evidence.own_voices: In 2016, she was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder
quality_evidence.nd_character: It doesn’t help that Stella has Asperger’s

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $22.00 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: It doesn’t help that Stella has Asperger’s and French kissing reminds her of a shark getting its teeth cleaned by pilot fish. Her conclusion: she needs lots of practice—with a professional.
entries.notes: Published by Berkley (Penguin Random House). An open-door romance with sex scenes; not for children.

entries.name: The Bride Test
entries.description: A romance about Khai, an autistic man who believes he cannot feel love, and Esme, who comes from Ho Chi Minh City to meet him as a possible bride. By an autistic author; for adults.

quality_evidence.own_voices: In 2016, she was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder
quality_evidence.nd_character: his autism means he just processes emotions differently

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $24.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: His family knows better—that his autism means he just processes emotions differently.
entries.notes: Published by Berkley (Penguin Random House). A companion to The Kiss Quotient, with sex scenes; not for children.

entries.name: The Maid
entries.description: A cozy locked-room mystery narrated by Molly, a young hotel maid who loves order and etiquette and becomes the police’s lead suspect when she finds a wealthy guest dead. Suits adults and older teens who like gentle crime fiction.

quality_evidence.nd_character: Molly is a likeable, neurodivergent narrator in this outstanding debut.

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $24.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Since Gran died a few months ago, twenty-five-year-old Molly has been navigating life’s complexities all by herself.
entries.notes: Published by Ballantine Books (Penguin Random House). The book does not name a diagnosis; the publisher’s page quotes a review calling Molly neurodivergent. Indigo tags it Canadian.

entries.name: An Unkindness of Ghosts
entries.description: A science-fiction novel about Aster, a neurodivergent healer enslaved on the lower decks of a generation starship, who uncovers secrets about her mother’s death. Dark and violent; for adults.

quality_evidence.nd_character: Aster is black, neuroatypical, ambiguously gendered

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $22.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Aster was born on the lower decks of the USS Matilda, a space vessel searching for a habitable planet after an ecological disaster on Earth.
entries.notes: Published by Akashic Books in 2017. The publisher’s page quotes a reviewer who lists it among stories with autistic protagonists and warns the characters are treated brutally.

entries.name: Motherless Brooklyn
entries.description: A literary detective novel narrated by Lionel Essrog, an amateur detective in Brooklyn who has Tourette’s syndrome. For adults who like crime fiction with a distinctive voice.

quality_evidence.nd_character: narrated by an amateur detective with Tourette’s syndrome

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $22.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: A half-satirical cross between a literary novel and a hard-boiled crime story narrated by an amateur detective with Tourette’s syndrome
entries.notes: Published by Vintage (Penguin Random House); National Book Critics Circle Award winner. The author is not described as having Tourette’s; in the publisher’s Q&A he says the Tourette’s community has been kind. Crime novel with violence.

entries.name: What Your Autistic Child Wants You to Know
entries.description: A guide for parents of autistic children and teens by an autistic psychologist, written with other autistic people. It covers mealtimes, bullying, social media, puberty, meltdowns and safe spaces, with advice from lived experience.

quality_evidence.own_voices: Written by autistic psychologist and advocate, Maja Toudal, in collaboration with other autistic voices
quality_evidence.for_parents: It can be challenging understanding what your autistic child wants and needs

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $30.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: this candid book explores a range of common situational and social challenges an autistic young person may face and gives lived-experience advice on how to resolve them.
entries.notes: Published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers (UK) in 2022; the publisher’s UK shop showed it as awaiting stock, but Indigo sells it in Canada.

entries.name: The Autistic Survival Guide to Therapy
entries.description: A guide to finding and using therapy as an autistic person, by a therapist who was diagnosed autistic late. It draws on her own experience, other therapists and the autistic community.

quality_evidence.own_voices: uses her professional and lived experiences as a late diagnosed autistic woman and therapist

entries.price_note: Prices vary by format and store; Indigo listed the paperback at $27.95 on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Steph Jones uses her professional and lived experiences as a late diagnosed autistic woman and therapist, as well as consulting therapists from across the world and tapping into the autistic community
entries.notes: Published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers (UK) in 2024. Useful for autistic adults and for therapists; the publisher’s UK shop showed it as awaiting stock.

entries.name: Tiimo
entries.description: A visual daily planner for ADHD and autistic people: tasks sit on a colour-coded timeline with timers, checklists and an AI helper to break tasks down. Free to start, with a Pro subscription for more features.

quality_evidence.nd_made: Tiimo was built by and for neurodivergent people from the start
quality_evidence.visual_supports: Visual Schedule Planner: Color-coded daily overview with easy drag-and-drop tasks.
quality_evidence.subscription: Auto-renewal can be canceled anytime via Apple settings.
quality_evidence.screen_reader: VoiceOver Navigate and explore the app using gestures, braille and speech output.
quality_evidence.ios: To-Do List Planner App - App Store

entries.price_note: Free with in-app purchases: the free version covers basic planning; Tiimo Pro is a subscription (Canadian App Store, 18 October 2026).
entries.evidence: Turn your schedule into a visual timeline you can actually follow.
entries.notes: Made in Copenhagen by Tiimo ApS. The site says Tiimo has been rebuilt for Android, but I could not confirm a Google Play listing, so only iPhone, iPad and Mac are claimed.

entries.name: Goblin Tools
entries.description: A set of small, single-task tools for overwhelm: Magic ToDo breaks a task into steps, and others change the tone of a message, guess how long an activity takes or explain things. Free on the website; the phone apps cost a few dollars once.

quality_evidence.web: Magic ToDo Break down todo items
quality_evidence.price_free: goblin.tools kept free by our sponsors
quality_evidence.ios: Goblin Tools App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Goblin Tools - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free on goblin.tools; the iPhone app is $2.99 and the Android app $1.59, with an optional Goblin Tools Pro subscription (Canadian stores, 18 October 2026).
entries.evidence: A collection of small, simple tools, for when things feel too big or complicated
entries.notes: The App Store page says it was “created with neurodivergent people in mind” and warns about copycat apps; only the Skyhook listing is official.

entries.name: Choiceworks
entries.description: A picture-board app for routines, waiting, choices and feelings, built by families with their own photos, words, video and recorded audio. Mainly for children, but also used by teens and adults who like visual structure.

quality_evidence.visual_supports: Visual supports families and schools can trust.
quality_evidence.customizable: create customized visual boards using pictures, text, video, and recorded audio
quality_evidence.for_children: Choiceworks helps children complete daily routines, understand and manage their feelings, and practice waiting
quality_evidence.for_parents: Families, caregivers, educators, and therapists can create customized visual boards
quality_evidence.no_ads: No ads · No trackers · No account
quality_evidence.screen_reader: VoiceOver Navigate and explore the app using gestures, braille and speech output.
quality_evidence.ios: Choiceworks App - App Store

entries.price_note: One-time price on the Canadian App Store (iPad) on 18 October 2026; the Android version is $10.99 on Google Play.
entries.evidence: We have been making visual supports for children and their families since 2005.
entries.notes: The iPad and Android versions have different prices. Bee Visual also makes Choiceworks Calendar, a separate app.

entries.name: Brili Routines
entries.description: A visual routine planner and timer for adults with ADHD that turns routines into timed, swipe-through steps. Needs a subscription after the free trial.

quality_evidence.for_adults: ADHD Time Management App For Adults
quality_evidence.visual_supports: Brili Routines is a visual planner and timekeeper
quality_evidence.ios: Brili Routines – Habit Tracker App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Brili Routines – Habit Tracker - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free to download with a free trial; subscriptions on the Canadian App Store ran from $6.99 to $10.49 a month or $34.99 to $66.99 a year on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Built for the Neurodivergent Community
entries.notes: Seller is Brili GmbH. The site’s wording (“help manage ADHD symptoms”, CBT practices) is about routines, not treatment.

entries.name: Structured
entries.description: A visual day planner that puts tasks, routines and habits on one clear timeline, to help reduce overwhelm. Free, with an optional Pro upgrade.

quality_evidence.visual_supports: A visual daily planner to organize tasks, routines, and habits.
quality_evidence.screen_reader: VoiceOver Navigate and explore the app using gestures, braille and speech output.
quality_evidence.ios: Structured: Daily Planner Todo App - App Store

entries.price_note: Free; Structured Pro is optional, by month, by year or as a one-time lifetime purchase ($99.99) on the Canadian App Store on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Structured combines all your tasks and to-dos into a single visual timeline.
entries.notes: Made by unorderly GmbH (Germany). An Android version exists, but I could not load its Google Play page, so Android is not claimed.

entries.name: Proloquo2Go
entries.description: A symbol-based AAC app for iPhone and iPad: people who cannot speak, or cannot always speak, tap symbols or type to speak with natural voices, including children’s voices. Vocabulary can grow from first words to full sentences.

quality_evidence.visual_supports: With more than 27,000 symbols, Proloquo2Go enables users with varying literacy levels to communicate effectively through easily recognizable images.
quality_evidence.for_children: enables nonspeaking children and adults to express themselves
quality_evidence.for_adults: enables nonspeaking children and adults to express themselves
quality_evidence.ios: Proloquo2Go AAC App - App Store

entries.price_note: Bought once on the Canadian App Store. It was half price ($179.99) from 14 to 21 October 2026 for AAC Awareness Month; see the App Store for today's price. An extra vocabulary is an optional in-app purchase.
entries.evidence: Proloquo2Go is an award-winning AAC app that enables nonspeaking children and adults to express themselves confidently and initiate conversations.
entries.notes: iOS only (iPhone, iPad, Mac). Made by AssistiveWare (Netherlands). Check the price after 21 October 2026.

entries.name: Proloquo4Text
entries.description: A text-to-speech AAC app for people who can read and write but cannot always speak, including autistic people. Everything is on one screen, with word prediction and saved phrases.

quality_evidence.for_adults: Children, teens and adults who can’t (always) speak can use this Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) app
quality_evidence.for_children: Children, teens and adults who can’t (always) speak can use this Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) app
quality_evidence.customizable: Versatile and customizable, you can use this app’s options and accessibility features to make it your own.
quality_evidence.ios: Proloquo4Text AAC App - App Store

entries.price_note: Bought once on the Canadian App Store. It was half price ($79.99) from 14 to 21 October 2026 for AAC Awareness Month; see the App Store for today's price.
entries.evidence: Proloquo4Text’s intuitive word and sentence prediction uses what you type to anticipate what you might say next
entries.notes: iOS only. The maker says it suits people who “can’t (always) speak”, which includes people who lose speech at times. Check the price after 21 October 2026.

entries.name: TouchChat HD - AAC with WordPower
entries.description: A full AAC app for iPad with ready-made vocabularies such as WordPower, symbol sets and many voices, used by people with autism, apraxia and other conditions that affect speech. A free 30-day trial runs through the TouchChat Discover app.

quality_evidence.customizable: Various synthesized and custom voice options are available
quality_evidence.captions: Captions Display the dialogue and relevant sounds of video or audio-only content with text, usually time-synchronized.
quality_evidence.ios: TouchChat HD- AAC w/ WordPower App - App Store

entries.price_note: Bought once on the Canadian App Store ($399.99 on 18 October 2026); extra vocabularies, symbol libraries and iShare backup subscriptions are in-app purchases.
entries.evidence: Using the familiarity of iOS technology, the TouchChat app offers you a dynamic communication
entries.notes: The App Store seller is Prentke Romich Company. The “Captions” label is the developer’s accessibility listing on the App Store. iOS only.

entries.name: Spoken - Tap to Talk AAC
entries.description: A typing-and-tapping AAC app for teens and adults who have trouble speaking, including nonspeaking autistic people, with word prediction and natural voices. Free to try, with a paid Premium plan.

quality_evidence.screen_reader: VoiceOver Navigate and explore the app using gestures, braille and speech output.
quality_evidence.ios: Spoken - Tap to Talk AAC App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Spoken – Tap to Talk AAC - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free to try; Premium is a subscription ($8.49 a month and up) or a lifetime purchase on the Canadian App Store on 18 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Spoken is an app designed for people unable to use their voice due to nonverbal autism, aphasia, stroke, or other speech and language disorders.
entries.notes: Uses the term “nonverbal autism”. The site says it uses AI-powered word predictions.

entries.name: Cboard
entries.description: A free, open-source picture-board AAC app that runs in a web browser and on Android, with symbols, text-to-speech and more than 45 languages. Boards can be edited for each person; it works offline in Chrome.

quality_evidence.price_free: Cboard is a free AAC web application
quality_evidence.works_offline: Offline support is available on Google Chrome (desktop & android).
quality_evidence.visual_supports: aiding communication with symbols and text-to-speech
quality_evidence.customizable: Cboard can be edited depending on the needs of each user.
quality_evidence.for_children: for children and adults with speech and language impairments
quality_evidence.for_adults: for children and adults with speech and language impairments
quality_evidence.android: Cboard AAC - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free; the Google Play listing shows optional in-app purchases.
entries.evidence: Cboard is an open-source app for children and adults with speech and language impairments, aiding communication with symbols and text-to-speech.
entries.notes: Open source; the Google Play package name suggests UNICEF support, but the pages I kept do not say so. No iOS app was checked.

entries.name: Avaz AAC
entries.description: A picture-and-text AAC app built around core words, for children and adults with autism and other conditions that affect speech. Free two-week trial, then a subscription or lifetime licence.

quality_evidence.customizable: Offers a variety of built-in options to add or change an icon’s image (or even video) right within the app.
quality_evidence.ios: Avaz AAC App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Avaz AAC - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free to download with a two-week trial; then a subscription ($13.99 a month or $134.99 a year) or a lifetime licence ($249.99) on the Canadian App Store on 19 October 2026.
entries.evidence: Avaz AAC is an Augmentative and Alternative Communication App that empowers children & adults with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Down Syndrome, Aphasia, Apraxia
entries.notes: Made by Avaz (with versions for India, Australia and French speakers). The evidence quote is from the maker’s App Store description.

entries.name: Forest
entries.description: A focus timer where a virtual tree grows while you stay off your phone and withers if you leave early, for Pomodoro-style work sessions. The App Store listing pitches it for ADHD focus. Free to start.

quality_evidence.ios: Forest: Focus for Productivity App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Forest: Stay Focused - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free to start, with in-app purchases including a subscription (Canadian App Store, 18 October 2026). The Android version contains ads.
entries.evidence: A mindful focus timer for intentional living — free to start
entries.notes: Seller: Seekrtech. Google Play says the Android version contains ads, so “no ads” is not claimed.

entries.name: Finch
entries.description: A self-care app where you look after a small virtual pet by doing small self-care steps such as goals, journaling and meditation. The main app is free; Finch Plus adds extras.

quality_evidence.price_free: a high-quality free version of Finch
quality_evidence.ios: Finch: Self-Care Pet App - App Store
quality_evidence.android: Finch: Self-Care Pet - Apps on Google Play

entries.price_note: Free; Finch Plus is optional (in-app purchases from $7.49 on the Canadian App Store, 18 October 2026).
entries.evidence: Daily self-care is finally fun — take care of your pet by taking care of yourself!
entries.notes: Made by Finch Care, a public benefit corporation. Not made for neurodivergent people in particular; the free-version quote is from the developer’s reply on the App Store.

entries.name: myNoise
